description: The (1+1)-ES minimises a function of real variables with one parent and one child per step. The child is the parent plus Gaussian noise of step size `σ`. It replaces the parent if it is not worse. The *1/5th success rule* controls `σ`: after a success `σ` grows by `exp(1/3)`, after a failure it shrinks by `exp(-1/12)`, so `σ` stays constant when exactly one child in five succeeds. It is simple and converges fast on smooth, unimodal functions; on multimodal functions it can stop in a local minimum.
